results.title: Schmid's question on isomorphic simple maximal subgroups (Kourovka 18.115)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that in every finite simple group $G$, any two isomorphic maximal subgroups $X$ and $Y$ that are themselves simple groups are conjugate in $\operatorname{Aut} G$, that is, $\varphi(X) = Y$ for some automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$.

results.title: Isomorphic simple maximal subgroups need not be conjugate under automorphisms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are a finite simple group $G$ and isomorphic maximal subgroups $X$ and $Y$ of $G$, both simple groups, such that no automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ satisfies $\varphi(X) = Y$. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 18.115 is negative.

results.title: Lower bound for Euler's function and upper bound for the sum of divisors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be Euler's totient function and $\sigma(n)$ the sum of the positive divisors of $n$. There is a constant $C > 0$ such that $\varphi(n)/n \ge C/\log\log n$ for every integer $n \ge 3$, and there is a constant $C'$ such that $\sigma(n)/n \le C' \log\log n$ for every integer $n \ge 3$.

results.title: Sieve bound for integers without small prime factors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $p(n)$ for the least prime factor of an integer $n \ge 2$, and set $p(1) = 1$. There is a constant $C$ such that for all real $x$ and $y$ with $2 \le y \le x$, the number of integers $1 \le n \le x$ with $p(n) > y$ is at most $C x / \log y$.

results.title: Integers with many prime factors are rare
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Omega(n)$ be the number of prime factors of $n$ counted with multiplicity. There is a constant $C$ such that for every real $x \ge 10$, the number of integers $1 \le n \le x$ with $\Omega(n) \ge 10 \log\log x$ is at most $C x / (\log x)^2$.

results.title: Integers whose sum of divisors has many divisors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\sigma(n)$ be the sum of the positive divisors of $n$ and $\tau(m)$ the number of positive divisors of $m$. There is a constant $C$ such that for every real $x \ge 10$, the number of integers $1 \le n \le x$ with $\tau(\sigma(n)) > \exp(\sqrt{\log x})$ is at most $C x / (\log x)^2$.

results.title: Benelux pairs of the first kind below $1.4 \cdot 10^{12}$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m < n$ be non-negative integers with $n < 1.4 \cdot 10^{12}$. Then $m$ and $n$ have the same prime factors and $m + 1$ and $n + 1$ have the same prime factors (that is, $(m, n)$ is a Benelux pair of the first kind) if and only if $(m, n) = (75, 1215)$ or $(m, n) = (2^k - 2, 2^{2k} - 2^{k+1})$ for some integer $k$ with $2 \le k \le 20$.

results.summary: Let $C_n = \binom{2n}{n} / (n + 1)$ be the $n$-th Catalan number. For a real number $\alpha$, there is a real sequence $(a_k)_{k \ge 0}$ with $a_{2k+1} = 0$ for every $k$ such that, for every $N \ge 0$, the difference $C_n \sqrt{\pi} \, (n + \alpha)^{3/2} / 4^n - \sum_{k=0}^{N} a_k (n + \alpha)^{-k}$ is $o\left((n + \alpha)^{-N}\right)$ as $n \to \infty$, if and only if $\alpha = 3/4$.

results.title: Blocks of the Smarandache permutation sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the $n$-th block is the list of the odd numbers $1, 3, \ldots, 2n - 1$ in increasing order followed by the even numbers $2n, 2n - 2, \ldots, 2$ in decreasing order; the $0$-th block is empty.

results.title: Prefix of the Smarandache permutation sequence
results.caption: Definition

For $N = 0$ it is the empty list.

results.title: Smarandache permutation sequence
results.caption: Definition

results.caption: Definition

results.title: Stirling-like matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $\alpha \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Q}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Stirling-like matrix $S_\alpha(n)$ is the $n \times n$ rational matrix, with rows and columns indexed by $1, \dots, n$, whose $(i, j)$ entry is $S_{i,j}$, where $S_{1,j} = \alpha_{j-1}$ for $j \ge 1$, $S_{i,1} = \alpha_0$ for $i \ge 2$, and $S_{i,j} = S_{i-1,j-1} + j \, S_{i-1,j}$ for $i, j \ge 2$.

results.title: The Vandermonde matrix $V(n)$

results.caption: Theorem
